{"draft": "Starbucks Q3 Fiscal 2026: Comparable Sales Strength Offsets China-Related Revenue Decline
Transaction-led comparable sales growth lifted earnings sharply even as consolidated revenue eased after the China transaction.
Consolidated net revenues slipped 1% to $9.3 billion, reflecting the conversion of the China retail business to a licensed joint venture model. Global comparable store sales climbed 7.9%, driven by a 4.2% increase in comparable transactions and a 3.5% increase in average ticket.
Profitability improved markedly. GAAP earnings per share rose 86% to $0.91, while non-GAAP earnings per share grew 70% to $0.85. GAAP operating margin expanded to 10.5%, and non-GAAP operating margin widened to 14.4%, helped by sales leverage and lower inflation paired with tariff refunds.
By segment, North America net revenues grew 7% to $7.4 billion, with operating margin reaching 13.6%. International net revenues fell 34% to $1.3 billion following the China conversion, while Channel Development net revenues jumped 22% to $587.9 million on strength in the Global Coffee Alliance.
The company used a portion of the China sale proceeds to complete tender offers to purchase approximately $1.3 billion aggregate principal amount of certain outstanding notes. The Board also declared a cash dividend of $0.62 per share.
Outlook: For the fourth quarter, the company expects U.S. comparable store sales growth of 6.5% or greater, leading to full fiscal year 2026 U.S. comparable store sales growth of slightly greater than 6.0%. It also guided to non-GAAP consolidated operating margin greater than 11.0% and non-GAAP earnings per share in the range of $2.55 to $2.65."}
